class.name: NetwInterestEngine
class.brief_description: The interest verdict core: mask algebra from plain state to a matrix saying which peers may see which entities.
class.description: A verdict is a function of state and of nothing else. This class reaches no [Object], reads no clock and emits no signal, so the same state always answers the same rows. Entity keys are opaque positive integers minted above this class and never dereferenced by it, which is what lets one entity outlive whichever handle, route or node is standing in for it. Peer bits are minted here by [method peer_bit_for], dense from zero and never reused, so a row keeps naming the peers it was computed for. [codeblock] set_layer / set_membership / set_parent ... mutations change intake state recompute() -> NetwInterestDelta computes, changes nothing commit(delta) advances the read matrix row_of / test / rows / explain read the committed matrix [/codeblock] One entity's row is granted by the union of its layers, or by every live peer when it belongs to none, then intersected with its synchronizer intent, then with its parent's row, then with the live peers. That parent clamp is the uniform-visibility invariant: a peer never holds a child whose parent it cannot see. Computing and committing are separate acts, so a caller can inspect a verdict before acting on it. A delta remembers the state it was computed against, and committing one that a later mutation has overtaken still applies, but leaves the mutation it did not see owed a further pass.

method.name: clear
method.description: Forgets every layer, entity, committed row, minted peer bit and counter. Session teardown.

method.name: commit
method.description: Advances the matrix that [method row_of], [method test] and [method rows] answer from, to what [param delta] computed.

method.name: declare_layer
method.description: Creates [param id] admitting nobody, if it does not already exist. A membership naming a layer is enough to create it, so this is for a layer that must exist before anybody joins it.

method.name: dirty_count
method.description: Entities owed a recompute. One mutation on a parent dirties its subtree, so this is not a count of mutations, and a caller keeping its own per-entity set would report a number the pass does not use.

method.name: explain
method.description: Names the first term that denies [param bit] to [param key], walking that entity's own intent and layers before climbing to its parent. Derived from the state the verdict used, so it cannot disagree with the row.

method.name: had_committed_intent
method.description: Whether the committed matrix was computed with an intent row for [param key]. Intake gains and loses one between passes, and what a committed row means is decided by the state it was computed against, so this answers from the commit rather than from [method has_intent].

method.name: has_entity
method.description: Whether intake currently holds [param key].

method.name: has_intent
method.description: Whether intake holds a synchronizer intent row for [param key], as opposed to the default of admitting every live peer. The two are different things: an intent row holding every live bit stops admitting a peer that joins later, and the default does not.

method.name: has_layer
method.description: Whether [param id] exists. A layer that does not exist admits nobody, which is not the same as one that admits everybody.

method.name: has_memberships
method.description: Whether [param key] names any layer. An entity naming none is granted by every live peer rather than by nobody, so this is not "is filtered" spelled differently.

method.name: intent_keys
method.description: Every entity intake holds an intent row for, in no particular order.

method.name: is_key
method.description: Whether [param key] may name an entity. Zero is what [method set_parent] spells "no parent" with, so an entity stored there could neither clamp nor be clamped, and every mutation refuses it.

method.name: known_peers
method.description: Every peer id that has been minted a bit, in bit order, so the entry at index [code]b[/code] is what [method peer_of_bit] answers for [code]b[/code].

method.name: layer_add_viewer
method.description: Adds [param peer_id] to [param id]'s viewer set, creating the layer if it is new, and answers whether the set changed. A caller that reports an edge on the answer reports it exactly when there was one. The bit is minted by [method peer_bit_for], so peer id [code]0[/code] is refused and answers [code]false[/code].

method.name: layer_admits
method.description: [param id]'s own verdict on [param peer_id]: its [method layer_policy] composed with viewer membership and nothing else. This is the term the matrix folds over a record's layers, answered on its own so a caller asking about one layer does not reconstruct the rule. A peer this engine has never minted a bit for is in no viewer set, and that is a verdict rather than an absence: [constant HIDE_FROM_INSIDERS] admits exactly those. Peer id [code]0[/code] names no participant and is refused under either policy.

method.name: layer_edge_count
method.description: Committed admitted pairs attributed to [param layer_id]. Counted from the committed memberships rather than from live intake, so the tally moves when a pass commits and not when a caller happens to mutate.

method.name: layer_explain
method.description: One line naming [method layer_admits]'s verdict, whether [param peer_id] is in the viewer set, and the [enum Policy] that composed them. It reads the same verdict rather than re-deriving one, so an explanation cannot disagree with the answer it explains. [codeblock] ADMIT peer=7 in viewers under HIDE_FROM_OUTSIDERS REJECT peer=9 not in viewers under HIDE_FROM_OUTSIDERS REJECT peer=0 (no peer context) [/codeblock]

method.name: layer_has_viewer
method.description: Whether [param id] views [param peer_id]. A layer or a peer this engine does not know views nothing, which fails closed.

method.name: layer_leave_policy
method.description: What [param id] declares its departure means on the wire, for an entity declaring no override of its own. A layer that does not exist answers [code]0[/code], which is DESPAWN.

method.name: layer_perception_policy
method.description: What [param id] declares its departure means to what the local player sees. A layer that does not exist answers [code]0[/code], which is HIDE.

method.name: layer_policy
method.description: [param id]'s [enum Policy]. A layer that does not exist answers [constant HIDE_FROM_OUTSIDERS], which is what a fresh one is created with.

method.name: layer_remove_viewer
method.description: Removes [param peer_id] from [param id]'s viewer set and answers whether the set changed. Removing a peer that is not there, or naming a layer that is not there, changes nothing.

method.name: layer_set_leave_policy
method.description: Declares [param id]'s default leave behaviour, creating the layer if it is new, and answers whether it changed. A policy outside [code]NetwMultiplayer.LeavePolicy[/code] is refused. No verdict composes this. It travels with the layer because there is nowhere else one layer's declaration could live without a second book to keep in step.

method.name: layer_set_perception_policy
method.description: Declares [param id]'s default local presentation behaviour, under the same rule as [method layer_set_leave_policy].

method.name: layer_set_policy
method.description: Replaces [param id]'s [enum Policy], creating the layer if it is new, and answers whether it changed.

method.name: layer_viewers
method.description: The peer ids [param id] views, in bit order. [method set_layer] writes bits rather than peer ids, so a row can hold a bit no peer was ever minted; such a bit still grants inside the algebra and is left out here, because it names nobody.

method.name: membership_add
method.description: Adds one membership and answers whether it changed anything. Naming a layer nobody has configured creates it admitting nobody, the same rule [method set_membership] follows.

method.name: membership_keys
method.description: Every entity intake holds a membership for, in no particular order. The caller that walks them is the one that knows what an entity is.

method.name: membership_remove
method.description: Removes one membership and answers whether it changed anything. Removing the last one leaves the entity granted by every live peer, which is a different thing from removing the entity.

method.name: memberships
method.description: [param key]'s memberships, in the order it joined them.

method.name: note_transition
method.description: Counts one show or hide edge [param id] reported. A monitor reads [method transitions] as a delta over an interval, so the count only ever grows.

method.name: order_route_for
method.description: An ordinal for an entity that has no route to be ordered by, minted on first ask and dense from one. Never reused, so an entity that leaves and comes back is ordered where it was rather than after everything minted since. [method clear] is the only thing that forgets one, and a key outside [method is_key] is refused with [code]0[/code]. It is what a caller hands [method set_order_key] as the route when the entity has none, and it exists because the route tiebreak has to be total even before a route.

method.name: peer_bit_for
method.description: The bit standing for [param peer_id] in every row, minted on first sight and answered unchanged forever after. Bits are dense from zero and are never reused, so a committed row keeps naming the peers it was computed for, and [method clear] is the only thing that forgets one. Peer id [code]0[/code] addresses nobody and is refused with [code]-1[/code], because a bit for it could not be told from an unknown one by [method peer_of_bit].

method.name: peer_bit_of
method.description: The bit [param peer_id] already holds, or [code]-1[/code]. Reading mints nothing, so asking about a peer this engine never saw does not enrol it.

method.name: peer_of_bit
method.description: The peer id [param bit] stands for, or [code]0[/code] when no peer holds it.

method.name: recompute
method.description: Computes the rows that would change, without touching the matrix readers see.

method.name: remove_entity
method.description: Removes [param key]. Its last act is a hide to every peer that held it, reported by the next [method recompute]. Its children are orphaned rather than left pointing at a record that is gone.

method.name: remove_layer
method.description: Removes [param id]. A membership naming a layer that is gone contributes nothing to the union, which is not the same as that layer admitting everyone.

method.name: roster
method.description: The entities enrolled in [param id] here, in the order they joined.

method.name: roster_add
method.description: Enrols [param key] in [param id], creating the layer if it is new, and answers whether it changed anything. This is NOT [method membership_add] spelled the other way round, and the difference is the point. A server enrols what it admits others to and holds a membership for it; a peer that computes no admission enrols what it was told it can see and holds no membership at all. One book derived from the other would answer for one of those two and not the other.

method.name: roster_has
method.description: Whether [param key] is enrolled in [param id].

method.name: roster_remove
method.description: Drops [param key] from [param id] and answers whether it changed anything.

method.name: row_after
method.description: The row [param key] will hold once [param delta] commits, answered while the old matrix still answers every other question.

method.name: row_of
method.description: The committed row for [param key], as packed peer-bit words. See [NetwInterestBitSet] for the packing.

method.name: rows
method.description: Every committed row, keyed by entity key.

method.name: set_intent
method.description: Replaces the synchronizer intent row for [param key], which intersects whatever its layers granted.

method.name: set_intent_all
method.description: Makes intent admit every live peer. Not the same as an intent row that happens to hold every live bit: this one survives a peer joining.

method.name: set_layer
method.description: Replaces one layer's viewer row and its [enum Policy]. Re-writing a layer with the values it already holds is inert, so an idempotent caller costs nothing.

method.name: set_live_peers
method.description: Replaces the row of currently live peer bits. Every row is intersected with it last, so a viewer bit for a peer that never joined cannot reach a committed row through any layer or intent.

method.name: set_membership
method.description: Replaces the layer memberships for [param key]. Naming a layer nobody has configured creates it admitting nobody, so an unconfigured layer is safe rather than transparent.

method.name: set_order_key
method.description: Replaces the [code](depth, route)[/code] pair transitions are ordered by. Two entities sharing one still order deterministically, broken by their keys.

method.name: set_parent
method.description: Replaces the parent of [param key]. A [param parent_key] of zero means no parent, and a link that would close a cycle is refused.

method.name: stats
method.description: The counters from the last committed pass.

method.name: test
method.description: Whether the committed row for [param key] admits [param bit].

method.name: transitions
method.description: Show plus hide edges [param id] has reported since it was declared. The count belongs to the layer rather than to its name, so a layer removed and named again starts from nothing.

method.name: viewer_peers
method.description: Every peer id any layer views, in bit order, unioned across the layers. Same rule as [method layer_viewers] for a bit that names nobody.

constants.constant: The layer admits the viewers it names, and nobody else.
The layer admits every live peer it does not name. Naming nobody admits everybody.
